node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:4:---
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:5:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:6:Fast refresh is a React feature integrated into Next.js that allows you to live reload the browser page while maintaining temporary client-side state when you save changes to a file. It's enabled by default in all Next.js applications on **9.4 or newer**. With Fast Refresh enabled, most edits should be visible within a second.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:7:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:8:## How It Works
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:9:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:10:- If you edit a file that **only exports React component(s)**, Fast Refresh will
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:11:  update the code only for that file, and re-render your component. You can edit
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:12:  anything in that file, including styles, rendering logic, event handlers, or
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:13:  effects.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:14:- If you edit a file with exports that _aren't_ React components, Fast Refresh
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:15:  will re-run both that file, and the other files importing it. So if both
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:16:  `Button.js` and `Modal.js` import `theme.js`, editing `theme.js` will update
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:17:  both components.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:18:- Finally, if you **edit a file** that's **imported by files outside of the
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:19:  React tree**, Fast Refresh **will fall back to doing a full reload**. You
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:20:  might have a file which renders a React component but also exports a value
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:21:  that is imported by a **non-React component**. For example, maybe your
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:22:  component also exports a constant, and a non-React utility file imports it. In
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:23:  that case, consider migrating the constant to a separate file and importing it
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:24:  into both files. This will re-enable Fast Refresh to work. Other cases can
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:25:  usually be solved in a similar way.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:26:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:27:## Error Resilience
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:28:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:29:### Syntax Errors
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:30:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:31:If you make a syntax error during development, you can fix it and save the file
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:32:again. The error will disappear automatically, so you won't need to reload the
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:33:app. **You will not lose component state**.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:34:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:35:### Runtime Errors
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:36:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:37:If you make a mistake that leads to a runtime error inside your component,
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:38:you'll be greeted with a contextual overlay. Fixing the error will automatically
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:39:dismiss the overlay, without reloading the app.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:40:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:41:Component state will be retained if the error did not occur during rendering. If
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:42:the error did occur during rendering, React will remount your application using
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:43:the updated code.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:44:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:45:If you have [error boundaries](https://react.dev/reference/react/Component#catching-rendering-errors-with-an-error-boundary)
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:46:in your app (which is a good idea for graceful failures in production), they
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:47:will retry rendering on the next edit after a rendering error. This means having
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:48:an error boundary can prevent you from always getting reset to the root app
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:49:state. However, keep in mind that error boundaries shouldn't be _too_ granular.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:50:They are used by React in production, and should always be designed
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:51:intentionally.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:52:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:53:## Limitations
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:54:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:55:Fast Refresh tries to preserve local React state in the component you're
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:56:editing, but only if it's safe to do so. Here's a few reasons why you might see
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:57:local state being reset on every edit to a file:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:58:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:59:- Local state is not preserved for class components (only function components
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:60:  and Hooks preserve state).
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:61:- The file you're editing might have _other_ exports in addition to a React
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:62:  component.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:63:- Sometimes, a file would export the result of calling a higher-order component
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:64:  like `HOC(WrappedComponent)`. If the returned component is a
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:65:  class, its state will be reset.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:66:- Anonymous arrow functions like `export default () => <div />;` cause Fast Refresh to not preserve local component state. For large codebases you can use our [`name-default-component` codemod](/docs/pages/guides/upgrading/codemods#name-default-component).
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:67:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:68:As more of your codebase moves to function components and Hooks, you can expect
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:69:state to be preserved in more cases.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:70:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:71:## Tips
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:72:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:73:- Fast Refresh preserves React local state in function components (and Hooks) by
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:74:  default.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:75:- Sometimes you might want to _force_ the state to be reset, and a component to
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:76:  be remounted. For example, this can be handy if you're tweaking an animation
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:77:  that only happens on mount. To do this, you can add `// @refresh reset`
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:78:  anywhere in the file you're editing. This directive is local to the file, and
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:79:  instructs Fast Refresh to remount components defined in that file on every
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:80:  edit.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:81:- You can put `console.log` or `debugger;` into the components you edit during
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:82:  development.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:83:- Remember that imports are case sensitive. Both fast and full refresh can fail,
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:84:  when your import doesn't match the actual filename.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:85:  For example, `'./header'` vs `'./Header'`.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:86:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:87:## Fast Refresh and Hooks
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:88:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:89:When possible, Fast Refresh attempts to preserve the state of your component
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:90:between edits. In particular, `useState` and `useRef` preserve their previous
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:91:values as long as you don't change their arguments or the order of the Hook
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:92:calls.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:93:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:94:Hooks with dependencies—such as `useEffect`, `useMemo`, and `useCallback`—will
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:95:_always_ update during Fast Refresh. Their list of dependencies will be ignored
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:96:while Fast Refresh is happening.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:97:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:98:For example, when you edit `useMemo(() => x * 2, [x])` to
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:99:`useMemo(() => x * 10, [x])`, it will re-run even though `x` (the dependency)
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:100:has not changed. If React didn't do that, your edit wouldn't reflect on the
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:101:screen!
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:102:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:103:Sometimes, this can lead to unexpected results. For example, even a `useEffect`
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:104:with an empty array of dependencies would still re-run once during Fast Refresh.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:105:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:106:However, writing code resilient to occasional re-running of `useEffect` is a good practice even
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:107:without Fast Refresh. It will make it easier for you to introduce new dependencies to it later on
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:108:and it's enforced by [React Strict Mode](/docs/pages/api-reference/config/next-config-js/reactStrictMode),
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:109:which we highly recommend enabling.

node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/instant-navigation.md:101:On a page load, the entire page renders from the document root. Every component runs on the server, and anything that suspends is caught by the nearest Suspense boundary in the full tree.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/instant-navigation.md:102:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/instant-navigation.md:103:On a client navigation (link click), Next.js only re-renders below the layout that the source and destination routes share. Components above that shared layout are not re-rendered. This means a Suspense boundary in the root layout covers everything on a page load, but for a client navigation between `/store/shoes` and `/store/hats`, the shared `/store` layout is the entry point. The root Suspense sits above it and has no effect.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/instant-navigation.md:104:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/instant-navigation.md:105:This is also why client-side hooks behave differently. `useSearchParams()` suspends during server rendering because search params are not available at build time. But on a client navigation, the router already has the params from the URL, so the hook resolves synchronously. The same component can appear in the instant shell on a client navigation but behind a fallback on a page load.

node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:16:## What is streaming?
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:17:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:18:In traditional server-side rendering, the server produces the full HTML document before sending anything. A single slow database query or API call can block the entire page. Streaming changes this by using [chunked transfer encoding](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Reference/Headers/Transfer-Encoding) to send parts of the response as they become ready. The browser starts rendering HTML while the server is still generating the rest.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:19:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:20:This is especially impactful for pages that combine fast static content (headers, navigation, layout) with slower dynamic content (personalized data, analytics, recommendations). The static parts can be prerendered and served from a CDN, painting instantly, while the dynamic parts stream in from the server as they become ready.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:21:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:22:React's server renderer produces HTML in chunks aligned with `<Suspense>` boundaries. Next.js integrates this into the App Router so streaming works without additional configuration.

node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:34:## How the App Router delivers a page
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:35:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:36:When a browser requests a page, two streams work together during the initial page load:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:37:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:38:### The HTML stream
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:39:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:40:React's server renderer produces progressive HTML chunks. The static parts of your page (layouts, navigation, Suspense fallbacks) render first and are sent immediately. When an async [Server Component](/docs/app/glossary#server-component) resolves, React streams its completed HTML along with inline `<script>` tags: one that swaps the fallback DOM node with the new content, and another carrying the [component payload](#the-component-payload) so React can later hydrate it. The browser executes the swap instantly, without waiting for the page's JavaScript bundle to load or hydration to complete. This is what the user _sees_: the page painting progressively, section by section.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:41:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:42:### The component payload
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:43:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:44:The component payload is a serialized representation of the component tree that React uses to [hydrate](/docs/app/glossary#hydration) the page and handle client-side updates. On initial load, it arrives embedded in the HTML stream (as described above). On **client-side navigation**, only the component payload is fetched (with an `rsc: 1` request header) and no HTML is transferred at all. React uses it to update the component tree in place.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:45:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:46:### The static shell
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:47:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:48:Everything that renders before any async work resolves is called the **static shell**: your layouts, navigation, and the fallback UI defined by your `<Suspense>` boundaries. It is sent immediately, giving the user something to see and interact with while dynamic content streams in. With [Cache Components](/docs/app/getting-started/caching), the static shell is prerendered at build time and served instantly from the edge.

node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:381:Prefer explicit `<Suspense>` boundaries close to the dynamic access. node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:574:## Streaming and Web Vitals
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:575:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:576:[Web Vitals](https://web.dev/articles/vitals) are the metrics Google uses to measure user experience. Streaming directly affects several of them.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:577:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:578:### TTFB and FCP
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:579:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:580:Without streaming, the server waits for all data before sending any HTML, so TTFB equals the slowest query. With streaming, the server sends the static shell as soon as it's ready. TTFB drops to the time it takes to render your layouts and fallbacks. The browser paints the static shell immediately, so FCP is decoupled from your data fetching time.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:581:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:582:### LCP (Largest Contentful Paint)
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:583:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:584:If your LCP element (a hero image, a main heading, a product photo) is inside a Suspense boundary, it can't paint until that boundary resolves. To keep LCP fast:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:585:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:586:- Keep LCP elements **outside** or **above** Suspense boundaries so they render as part of the static shell.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:587:- Use the [`preload`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/image#preload) prop on `next/image` for LCP images. This injects a `<link rel="preload">` into the `<head>`, so the browser starts fetching the image from the very first chunk, before the `<img>` tag even appears in the HTML.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:588:- For non-image LCP elements (text, headings), make sure they are not wrapped in a Suspense boundary that depends on slow data.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:589:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:590:### CLS (Cumulative Layout Shift)
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:591:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:592:When a Suspense fallback is replaced by the resolved content, the browser reflows the page. If the fallback and the resolved content are different sizes, the surrounding layout shifts. To minimize CLS:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:593:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:594:- Design skeleton fallbacks that **match the dimensions** of the content they represent. A skeleton with the same height and width as the final card grid prevents shifts.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:595:- Use fixed or min-height containers around Suspense boundaries so the space is reserved before content arrives.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:596:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:597:### INP (Interaction to Next Paint)
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:598:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:599:Streaming enables [selective hydration](https://react.dev/reference/react-dom/client/hydrateRoot): React hydrates components independently as they stream in, and prioritizes hydrating whatever the user is interacting with. Each `<Suspense>` boundary is a hydration unit. Without them, React hydrates the entire page in one blocking pass. With them, hydration is broken into smaller tasks that yield to the browser, keeping the main thread responsive. The [companion demo](https://streaming-demo.labs.vercel.dev/hydration-single) lets you compare a single blocking hydration pass with [split hydration](https://streaming-demo.labs.vercel.dev/hydration-split) using Suspense boundaries.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:600:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:601:### Early resource discovery
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:602:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:603:The static shell includes `<link>` and `<script>` tags in the very first HTML chunk. The browser discovers and starts fetching CSS, JavaScript, and fonts immediately, while the server is still generating content. Resources are fetched during server think time rather than after it.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:604:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:605:In the [dashboard example](#parallel-streaming-with-sibling-boundaries) above, the `<h1>` renders in the shell (good for LCP), each data section streams independently behind its own Suspense boundary (good for INP since hydration is split), and the skeleton fallbacks reserve space (good for CLS).
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:606:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:607:## The HTTP contract
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:608:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:609:Once streaming begins, the HTTP response headers (including the status code) have already been sent to the client. **You cannot change the status code or headers after streaming starts.** Everything in this section flows from this fundamental constraint.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:610:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:611:### Status codes
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:612:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:613:When a `<Suspense>` fallback renders or a component suspends, the server must commit to `200 OK` in order to start sending the HTML stream. If a [`notFound()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/not-found) fires mid-stream, Next.js cannot go back and change the status to 404. Instead, it injects `<meta name="robots" content="noindex">` into the streamed HTML so that search engines don't index the page. Similarly, a [`redirect()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/redirect) mid-stream becomes a client-side redirect rather than an HTTP redirect header.

node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:780:The trigger is **your code**: async work, non-deterministic output, or runtime data. When the framework encounters these, it walks up the tree looking for a `<Suspense>` boundary to use as a fallback. node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:782:The key decisions are **what to cache** and **where to place Suspense boundaries**. node_modules/next/dist/docs/04-community/01-contribution-guide.md:388:## Style Guide
node_modules/next/dist/docs/04-community/01-contribution-guide.md:389:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/04-community/01-contribution-guide.md:390:This section contains guidelines for writing docs for those who are new to technical writing.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/04-community/01-contribution-guide.md:391:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/04-community/01-contribution-guide.md:392:### Page Templates
node_modules/next/dist/docs/04-community/01-contribution-guide.md:393:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/04-community/01-contribution-guide.md:394:While we don't have a strict template for pages, there are page sections you'll see repeated across the docs:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/04-community/01-contribution-guide.md:395:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/04-community/01-contribution-guide.md:396:- **Overview:** The first paragraph of a page should tell the user what the feature is and what it's used for. Followed by a minimum working example or its API reference.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/04-community/01-contribution-guide.md:397:- **Convention:** If the feature has a convention, it should be explained here.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/04-community/01-contribution-guide.md:398:- **Examples**: Show how the feature can be used with different use cases.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/04-community/01-contribution-guide.md:399:- **API Tables**: API Pages should have an overview table at the of the page with jump-to-section links (when possible).
node_modules/next/dist/docs/04-community/01-contribution-guide.md:400:- **Next Steps (Related Links)**: Add links to related pages to guide the user's learning journey.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/04-community/01-contribution-guide.md:401:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/04-community/01-contribution-guide.md:402:Feel free to add these sections as needed.

node_modules/next/dist/docs/04-community/01-contribution-guide.md:404:### Page Types
node_modules/next/dist/docs/04-community/01-contribution-guide.md:405:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/04-community/01-contribution-guide.md:406:Docs pages are also split into two categories: Conceptual and Reference.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/04-community/01-contribution-guide.md:407:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/04-community/01-contribution-guide.md:408:- **Conceptual** pages are used to explain a concept or feature. They are usually longer and contain more information than reference pages. In the Next.js docs, conceptual pages are found in the **Building Your Application** section.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/04-community/01-contribution-guide.md:409:- **Reference** pages are used to explain a specific API. They are usually shorter and more focused. In the Next.js docs, reference pages are found in the **API Reference** section.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/04-community/01-contribution-guide.md:410:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/04-community/01-contribution-guide.md:411:> **Good to know**: Depending on the page you're contributing to, you may need to follow a different voice and style. For example, conceptual pages are more instructional and use the word _you_ to address the user. Reference pages are more technical, they use more imperative words like "create, update, accept" and tend to omit the word _you_.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/04-community/01-contribution-guide.md:412:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/04-community/01-contribution-guide.md:413:### Voice
node_modules/next/dist/docs/04-community/01-contribution-guide.md:414:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/04-community/01-contribution-guide.md:415:Here are some guidelines to maintain a consistent style and voice across the docs:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/04-community/01-contribution-guide.md:416:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/04-community/01-contribution-guide.md:417:- Write clear, concise sentences. Avoid tangents.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/04-community/01-contribution-guide.md:418:  - If you find yourself using a lot of commas, consider breaking the sentence into multiple sentences or use a list.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/04-community/01-contribution-guide.md:419:  - Swap out complex words for simpler ones. For example, _use_ instead of _utilize_.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/04-community/01-contribution-guide.md:420:- Be mindful with the word _this_. It can be ambiguous and confusing, don't be afraid to repeat the subject of the sentence if unclear.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/04-community/01-contribution-guide.md:421:  - For example, _Next.js uses React_ instead of _Next.js uses this_.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/04-community/01-contribution-guide.md:422:- Use an active voice instead of passive. An active sentence is easier to read.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/04-community/01-contribution-guide.md:423:  - For example, _Next.js uses React_ instead of _React is used by Next.js_. If you find yourself using words like _was_ and _by_ you may be using a passive voice.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/04-community/01-contribution-guide.md:424:- Avoid using words like _easy_, _quick_, _simple_, _just_, etc. This is subjective and can be discouraging to users.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/04-community/01-contribution-guide.md:425:- Avoid negative words like _don't_, _can't_, _won't_, etc. This can be discouraging to readers.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/04-community/01-contribution-guide.md:426:  - For example, _"You can use the `Link` component to create links between pages"_ instead of _"Don't use the `<a>` tag to create links between pages"_.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/04-community/01-contribution-guide.md:427:- Write in second person (you/your). This is more personal and engaging.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/04-community/01-contribution-guide.md:428:- Use gender-neutral language. Use _developers_, _users_, or _readers_, when referring to the audience.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/04-community/01-contribution-guide.md:429:- If adding code examples, ensure they are properly formatted and working.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/04-community/01-contribution-guide.md:430:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/04-community/01-contribution-guide.md:431:While these guidelines are not exhaustive, they should help you get started. If you'd like to dive deeper into technical writing, check out the [Google Technical Writing Course](https://developers.google.com/tech-writing/overview).

node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:2:title: Fast Refresh
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:3:description: Fast Refresh is a hot module reloading experience that gives you instantaneous feedback on edits made to your React components.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:4:---
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:5:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:6:Fast refresh is a React feature integrated into Next.js that allows you to live reload the browser page while maintaining temporary client-side state when you save changes to a file. It's enabled by default in all Next.js applications on **9.4 or newer**. With Fast Refresh enabled, most edits should be visible within a second.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:7:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:8:## How It Works
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:9:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:10:- If you edit a file that **only exports React component(s)**, Fast Refresh will
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:11:  update the code only for that file, and re-render your component. You can edit
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:12:  anything in that file, including styles, rendering logic, event handlers, or
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:13:  effects.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:14:- If you edit a file with exports that _aren't_ React components, Fast Refresh
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:15:  will re-run both that file, and the other files importing it. So if both
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:16:  `Button.js` and `Modal.js` import `theme.js`, editing `theme.js` will update
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:17:  both components.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:18:- Finally, if you **edit a file** that's **imported by files outside of the
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:19:  React tree**, Fast Refresh **will fall back to doing a full reload**. You
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:20:  might have a file which renders a React component but also exports a value
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:21:  that is imported by a **non-React component**. For example, maybe your
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:22:  component also exports a constant, and a non-React utility file imports it. In
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:23:  that case, consider migrating the constant to a separate file and importing it
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:24:  into both files. This will re-enable Fast Refresh to work. Other cases can
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:25:  usually be solved in a similar way.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:26:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:27:## Error Resilience
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:28:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:29:### Syntax Errors
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:30:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:31:If you make a syntax error during development, you can fix it and save the file
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:32:again. The error will disappear automatically, so you won't need to reload the
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:33:app. **You will not lose component state**.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:34:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:35:### Runtime Errors
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:36:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:37:If you make a mistake that leads to a runtime error inside your component,
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:38:you'll be greeted with a contextual overlay. Fixing the error will automatically
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:39:dismiss the overlay, without reloading the app.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:40:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:41:Component state will be retained if the error did not occur during rendering. If
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:42:the error did occur during rendering, React will remount your application using
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:43:the updated code.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:44:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:45:If you have [error boundaries](https://react.dev/reference/react/Component#catching-rendering-errors-with-an-error-boundary)
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:46:in your app (which is a good idea for graceful failures in production), they
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:47:will retry rendering on the next edit after a rendering error. This means having
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:48:an error boundary can prevent you from always getting reset to the root app
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:49:state. However, keep in mind that error boundaries shouldn't be _too_ granular.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:50:They are used by React in production, and should always be designed
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:51:intentionally.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:52:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:53:## Limitations
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:54:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:55:Fast Refresh tries to preserve local React state in the component you're
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:56:editing, but only if it's safe to do so. Here's a few reasons why you might see
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:57:local state being reset on every edit to a file:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:58:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:59:- Local state is not preserved for class components (only function components
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:60:  and Hooks preserve state).
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:61:- The file you're editing might have _other_ exports in addition to a React
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:62:  component.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:63:- Sometimes, a file would export the result of calling a higher-order component
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:64:  like `HOC(WrappedComponent)`. If the returned component is a
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:65:  class, its state will be reset.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:66:- Anonymous arrow functions like `export default () => <div />;` cause Fast Refresh to not preserve local component state. For large codebases you can use our [`name-default-component` codemod](/docs/pages/guides/upgrading/codemods#name-default-component).
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:67:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:68:As more of your codebase moves to function components and Hooks, you can expect
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:69:state to be preserved in more cases.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:70:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:71:## Tips
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:72:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:73:- Fast Refresh preserves React local state in function components (and Hooks) by
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:74:  default.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:75:- Sometimes you might want to _force_ the state to be reset, and a component to
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:76:  be remounted. For example, this can be handy if you're tweaking an animation
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:77:  that only happens on mount. To do this, you can add `// @refresh reset`
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:78:  anywhere in the file you're editing. This directive is local to the file, and
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:79:  instructs Fast Refresh to remount components defined in that file on every
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:80:  edit.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:81:- You can put `console.log` or `debugger;` into the components you edit during
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:82:  development.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:83:- Remember that imports are case sensitive. Both fast and full refresh can fail,
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:84:  when your import doesn't match the actual filename.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:85:  For example, `'./header'` vs `'./Header'`.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:86:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:87:## Fast Refresh and Hooks
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:88:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:89:When possible, Fast Refresh attempts to preserve the state of your component
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:90:between edits. In particular, `useState` and `useRef` preserve their previous
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:91:values as long as you don't change their arguments or the order of the Hook
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:92:calls.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:93:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:94:Hooks with dependencies—such as `useEffect`, `useMemo`, and `useCallback`—will
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:95:_always_ update during Fast Refresh. Their list of dependencies will be ignored
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:96:while Fast Refresh is happening.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:97:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:98:For example, when you edit `useMemo(() => x * 2, [x])` to
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:99:`useMemo(() => x * 10, [x])`, it will re-run even though `x` (the dependency)
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:100:has not changed. If React didn't do that, your edit wouldn't reflect on the
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:101:screen!
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:102:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:103:Sometimes, this can lead to unexpected results. For example, even a `useEffect`

node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/instant-navigation.md:101:On a page load, the entire page renders from the document root. Every component runs on the server, and anything that suspends is caught by the nearest Suspense boundary in the full tree.

node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/instant-navigation.md:103:On a client navigation (link click), Next.js only re-renders below the layout that the source and destination routes share. Components above that shared layout are not re-rendered. This means a Suspense boundary in the root layout covers everything on a page load, but for a client navigation between `/store/shoes` and `/store/hats`, the shared `/store` layout is the entry point. The root Suspense sits above it and has no effect.

node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:16:## What is streaming?
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:17:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:18:In traditional server-side rendering, the server produces the full HTML document before sending anything. A single slow database query or API call can block the entire page. Streaming changes this by using [chunked transfer encoding](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Reference/Headers/Transfer-Encoding) to send parts of the response as they become ready. The browser starts rendering HTML while the server is still generating the rest.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:19:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:20:This is especially impactful for pages that combine fast static content (headers, navigation, layout) with slower dynamic content (personalized data, analytics, recommendations). The static parts can be prerendered and served from a CDN, painting instantly, while the dynamic parts stream in from the server as they become ready.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:21:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:22:React's server renderer produces HTML in chunks aligned with `<Suspense>` boundaries. Next.js integrates this into the App Router so streaming works without additional configuration.

node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:34:## How the App Router delivers a page
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:35:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:36:When a browser requests a page, two streams work together during the initial page load:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:37:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:38:### The HTML stream
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:39:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:40:React's server renderer produces progressive HTML chunks. The static parts of your page (layouts, navigation, Suspense fallbacks) render first and are sent immediately. When an async [Server Component](/docs/app/glossary#server-component) resolves, React streams its completed HTML along with inline `<script>` tags: one that swaps the fallback DOM node with the new content, and another carrying the [component payload](#the-component-payload) so React can later hydrate it. The browser executes the swap instantly, without waiting for the page's JavaScript bundle to load or hydration to complete. This is what the user _sees_: the page painting progressively, section by section.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:41:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:42:### The component payload
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:43:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:44:The component payload is a serialized representation of the component tree that React uses to [hydrate](/docs/app/glossary#hydration) the page and handle client-side updates. On initial load, it arrives embedded in the HTML stream (as described above). On **client-side navigation**, only the component payload is fetched (with an `rsc: 1` request header) and no HTML is transferred at all. React uses it to update the component tree in place.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:45:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:46:### The static shell
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:47:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:48:Everything that renders before any async work resolves is called the **static shell**: your layouts, navigation, and the fallback UI defined by your `<Suspense>` boundaries. It is sent immediately, giving the user something to see and interact with while dynamic content streams in. With [Cache Components](/docs/app/getting-started/caching), the static shell is prerendered at build time and served instantly from the edge.

node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:574:## Streaming and Web Vitals
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:575:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:576:[Web Vitals](https://web.dev/articles/vitals) are the metrics Google uses to measure user experience. Streaming directly affects several of them.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:577:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:578:### TTFB and FCP
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:579:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:580:Without streaming, the server waits for all data before sending any HTML, so TTFB equals the slowest query. With streaming, the server sends the static shell as soon as it's ready. TTFB drops to the time it takes to render your layouts and fallbacks. The browser paints the static shell immediately, so FCP is decoupled from your data fetching time.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:581:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:582:### LCP (Largest Contentful Paint)
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:583:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:584:If your LCP element (a hero image, a main heading, a product photo) is inside a Suspense boundary, it can't paint until that boundary resolves. To keep LCP fast:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:585:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:586:- Keep LCP elements **outside** or **above** Suspense boundaries so they render as part of the static shell.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:587:- Use the [`preload`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/image#preload) prop on `next/image` for LCP images. This injects a `<link rel="preload">` into the `<head>`, so the browser starts fetching the image from the very first chunk, before the `<img>` tag even appears in the HTML.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:588:- For non-image LCP elements (text, headings), make sure they are not wrapped in a Suspense boundary that depends on slow data.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:589:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:590:### CLS (Cumulative Layout Shift)
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:591:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:592:When a Suspense fallback is replaced by the resolved content, the browser reflows the page. If the fallback and the resolved content are different sizes, the surrounding layout shifts. To minimize CLS:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:593:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:594:- Design skeleton fallbacks that **match the dimensions** of the content they represent. A skeleton with the same height and width as the final card grid prevents shifts.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:595:- Use fixed or min-height containers around Suspense boundaries so the space is reserved before content arrives.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:596:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:597:### INP (Interaction to Next Paint)
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:598:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:599:Streaming enables [selective hydration](https://react.dev/reference/react-dom/client/hydrateRoot): React hydrates components independently as they stream in, and prioritizes hydrating whatever the user is interacting with. Each `<Suspense>` boundary is a hydration unit. Without them, React hydrates the entire page in one blocking pass. With them, hydration is broken into smaller tasks that yield to the browser, keeping the main thread responsive. The [companion demo](https://streaming-demo.labs.vercel.dev/hydration-single) lets you compare a single blocking hydration pass with [split hydration](https://streaming-demo.labs.vercel.dev/hydration-split) using Suspense boundaries.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:600:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:601:### Early resource discovery
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:602:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:603:The static shell includes `<link>` and `<script>` tags in the very first HTML chunk. node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:605:In the [dashboard example](#parallel-streaming-with-sibling-boundaries) above, the `<h1>` renders in the shell (good for LCP), each data section streams independently behind its own Suspense boundary (good for INP since hydration is split), and the skeleton fallbacks reserve space (good for CLS).

node_modules/next/dist/docs/02-pages/03-building-your-application/03-data-fetching/05-client-side.md:3:description: Learn about client-side data fetching, and how to use SWR, a data fetching React Hook library that handles caching, revalidation, focus tracking, refetching on interval and more.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/02-pages/03-building-your-application/03-data-fetching/05-client-side.md:4:---

node_modules/next/dist/docs/02-pages/03-building-your-application/03-data-fetching/05-client-side.md:6:Client-side data fetching is useful when your page doesn't require SEO indexing, when you don't need to prerender your data, or when the content of your pages needs to update frequently. Unlike the server-side rendering APIs, you can use client-side data fetching at the component level.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/02-pages/03-building-your-application/03-data-fetching/05-client-side.md:7:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/02-pages/03-building-your-application/03-data-fetching/05-client-side.md:8:If done at the page level, the data is fetched at runtime, and the content of the page is updated as the data changes. When used at the component level, the data is fetched at the time of the component mount, and the content of the component is updated as the data changes.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/02-pages/03-building-your-application/03-data-fetching/05-client-side.md:9:

node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:27:## Error Resilience
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:28:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:29:### Syntax Errors
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:30:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:31:If you make a syntax error during development, you can fix it and save the file
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:32:again. The error will disappear automatically, so you won't need to reload the
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:33:app. **You will not lose component state**.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:34:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:35:### Runtime Errors
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:36:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:37:If you make a mistake that leads to a runtime error inside your component,

node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:39:dismiss the overlay, without reloading the app.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:40:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:41:Component state will be retained if the error did not occur during rendering. If
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:42:the error did occur during rendering, React will remount your application using
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:43:the updated code.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:44:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:45:If you have [error boundaries](https://react.dev/reference/react/Component#catching-rendering-errors-with-an-error-boundary)
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:46:in your app (which is a good idea for graceful failures in production), they
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:47:will retry rendering on the next edit after a rendering error. This means having
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:48:an error boundary can prevent you from always getting reset to the root app
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:49:state. However, keep in mind that error boundaries shouldn't be _too_ granular.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:50:They are used by React in production, and should always be designed

node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:52:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:53:## Limitations
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:54:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:55:Fast Refresh tries to preserve local React state in the component you're
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:56:editing, but only if it's safe to do so. Here's a few reasons why you might see
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:57:local state being reset on every edit to a file:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:58:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:59:- Local state is not preserved for class components (only function components
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:60:  and Hooks preserve state).
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:61:- The file you're editing might have _other_ exports in addition to a React
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:62:  component.

node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:65:  class, its state will be reset.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:66:- Anonymous arrow functions like `export default () => <div />;` cause Fast Refresh to not preserve local component state. For large codebases you can use our [`name-default-component` codemod](/docs/pages/guides/upgrading/codemods#name-default-component).

node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:68:As more of your codebase moves to function components and Hooks, you can expect
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:69:state to be preserved in more cases.

node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:71:## Tips
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:72:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:73:- Fast Refresh preserves React local state in function components (and Hooks) by
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:74:  default.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:75:- Sometimes you might want to _force_ the state to be reset, and a component to
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:76:  be remounted. For example, this can be handy if you're tweaking an animation
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:77:  that only happens on mount. To do this, you can add `// @refresh reset`
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:78:  anywhere in the file you're editing. This directive is local to the file, and

node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:80:  edit.

node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:82:  development.

node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:86:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:87:## Fast Refresh and Hooks
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:88:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:89:When possible, Fast Refresh attempts to preserve the state of your component
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:90:between edits. In particular, `useState` and `useRef` preserve their previous
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:91:values as long as you don't change their arguments or the order of the Hook
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:92:calls.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:93:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:94:Hooks with dependencies—such as `useEffect`, `useMemo`, and `useCallback`—will
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:95:_always_ update during Fast Refresh. Their list of dependencies will be ignored
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:96:while Fast Refresh is happening.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:97:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:98:For example, when you edit `useMemo(() => x * 2, [x])` to
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:99:`useMemo(() => x * 10, [x])`, it will re-run even though `x` (the dependency)
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:100:has not changed. If React didn't do that, your edit wouldn't reflect on the
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:101:screen!
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:102:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:103:Sometimes, this can lead to unexpected results. For example, even a `useEffect`
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:104:with an empty array of dependencies would still re-run once during Fast Refresh.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:105:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:106:However, writing code resilient to occasional re-running of `useEffect` is a good practice even
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:107:without Fast Refresh. It will make it easier for you to introduce new dependencies to it later on
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:108:and it's enforced by [React Strict Mode](/docs/pages/api-reference/config/next-config-js/reactStrictMode),
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:109:which we highly recommend enabling.

node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:16:## What is streaming?
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:17:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:18:In traditional server-side rendering, the server produces the full HTML document before sending anything. A single slow database query or API call can block the entire page. Streaming changes this by using [chunked transfer encoding](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Reference/Headers/Transfer-Encoding) to send parts of the response as they become ready. The browser starts rendering HTML while the server is still generating the rest.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:19:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:20:This is especially impactful for pages that combine fast static content (headers, navigation, layout) with slower dynamic content (personalized data, analytics, recommendations). The static parts can be prerendered and served from a CDN, painting instantly, while the dynamic parts stream in from the server as they become ready.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:21:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:22:React's server renderer produces HTML in chunks aligned with `<Suspense>` boundaries. Next.js integrates this into the App Router so streaming works without additional configuration.

node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:34:## How the App Router delivers a page
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:35:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:36:When a browser requests a page, two streams work together during the initial page load:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:37:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:38:### The HTML stream
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:39:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:40:React's server renderer produces progressive HTML chunks. The static parts of your page (layouts, navigation, Suspense fallbacks) render first and are sent immediately. When an async [Server Component](/docs/app/glossary#server-component) resolves, React streams its completed HTML along with inline `<script>` tags: one that swaps the fallback DOM node with the new content, and another carrying the [component payload](#the-component-payload) so React can later hydrate it. The browser executes the swap instantly, without waiting for the page's JavaScript bundle to load or hydration to complete. This is what the user _sees_: the page painting progressively, section by section.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:41:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:42:### The component payload
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:43:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:44:The component payload is a serialized representation of the component tree that React uses to [hydrate](/docs/app/glossary#hydration) the page and handle client-side updates. On initial load, it arrives embedded in the HTML stream (as described above). On **client-side navigation**, only the component payload is fetched (with an `rsc: 1` request header) and no HTML is transferred at all. React uses it to update the component tree in place.

node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:46:### The static shell

node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:48:Everything that renders before any async work resolves is called the **static shell**: your layouts, navigation, and the fallback UI defined by your `<Suspense>` boundaries. It is sent immediately, giving the user something to see and interact with while dynamic content streams in. With [Cache Components](/docs/app/getting-started/caching), the static shell is prerendered at build time and served instantly from the edge.

node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:578:### TTFB and FCP

node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:580:Without streaming, the server waits for all data before sending any HTML, so TTFB equals the slowest query. node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:582:### LCP (Largest Contentful Paint)
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:583:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:584:If your LCP element (a hero image, a main heading, a product photo) is inside a Suspense boundary, it can't paint until that boundary resolves. To keep LCP fast:

node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:590:### CLS (Cumulative Layout Shift)

node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:592:When a Suspense fallback is replaced by the resolved content, the browser reflows the page. If the fallback and the resolved content are different sizes, the surrounding layout shifts. To minimize CLS:

node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:595:- Use fixed or min-height containers around Suspense boundaries so the space is reserved before content arrives.

node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:597:### INP (Interaction to Next Paint)
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:598:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:599:Streaming enables [selective hydration](https://react.dev/reference/react-dom/client/hydrateRoot): React hydrates components independently as they stream in, and prioritizes hydrating whatever the user is interacting with. node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:3:description: Fast Refresh is a hot module reloading experience that gives you instantaneous feedback on edits made to your React components.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:4:---
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:5:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:6:Fast refresh is a React feature integrated into Next.js that allows you to live reload the browser page while maintaining temporary client-side state when you save changes to a file. It's enabled by default in all Next.js applications on **9.4 or newer**. With Fast Refresh enabled, most edits should be visible within a second.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:7:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:8:## How It Works
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:9:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:10:- If you edit a file that **only exports React component(s)**, Fast Refresh will
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:11:  update the code only for that file, and re-render your component. You can edit
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:12:  anything in that file, including styles, rendering logic, event handlers, or
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:13:  effects.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:14:- If you edit a file with exports that _aren't_ React components, Fast Refresh
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:15:  will re-run both that file, and the other files importing it. So if both
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:16:  `Button.js` and `Modal.js` import `theme.js`, editing `theme.js` will update
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:17:  both components.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:18:- Finally, if you **edit a file** that's **imported by files outside of the
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:19:  React tree**, Fast Refresh **will fall back to doing a full reload**. You
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:20:  might have a file which renders a React component but also exports a value
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:21:  that is imported by a **non-React component**. For example, maybe your
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:22:  component also exports a constant, and a non-React utility file imports it. In
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:23:  that case, consider migrating the constant to a separate file and importing it
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:24:  into both files. This will re-enable Fast Refresh to work. Other cases can
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:25:  usually be solved in a similar way.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:26:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:27:## Error Resilience
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:28:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:29:### Syntax Errors
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:30:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:31:If you make a syntax error during development, you can fix it and save the file
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:32:again. The error will disappear automatically, so you won't need to reload the
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:33:app. **You will not lose component state**.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:34:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:35:### Runtime Errors
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:36:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:37:If you make a mistake that leads to a runtime error inside your component,
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:38:you'll be greeted with a contextual overlay. Fixing the error will automatically
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:39:dismiss the overlay, without reloading the app.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:40:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:41:Component state will be retained if the error did not occur during rendering. If
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:42:the error did occur during rendering, React will remount your application using
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:43:the updated code.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:44:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:45:If you have [error boundaries](https://react.dev/reference/react/Component#catching-rendering-errors-with-an-error-boundary)
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:46:in your app (which is a good idea for graceful failures in production), they
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:47:will retry rendering on the next edit after a rendering error. This means having
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:48:an error boundary can prevent you from always getting reset to the root app
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:49:state. However, keep in mind that error boundaries shouldn't be _too_ granular.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:50:They are used by React in production, and should always be designed
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:51:intentionally.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:52:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:53:## Limitations
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:54:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:55:Fast Refresh tries to preserve local React state in the component you're
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:56:editing, but only if it's safe to do so. Here's a few reasons why you might see
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:57:local state being reset on every edit to a file:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:58:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:59:- Local state is not preserved for class components (only function components
node_modules/next/dist/docs/03-architecture/fast-refresh.md:60:  and Hooks preserve state).

node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:16:## What is streaming?
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:17:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:18:In traditional server-side rendering, the server produces the full HTML document before sending anything. A single slow database query or API call can block the entire page. Streaming changes this by using [chunked transfer encoding](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Reference/Headers/Transfer-Encoding) to send parts of the response as they become ready. The browser starts rendering HTML while the server is still generating the rest.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:19:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:20:This is especially impactful for pages that combine fast static content (headers, navigation, layout) with slower dynamic content (personalized data, analytics, recommendations). The static parts can be prerendered and served from a CDN, painting instantly, while the dynamic parts stream in from the server as they become ready.

node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:22:React's server renderer produces HTML in chunks aligned with `<Suspense>` boundaries. Next.js integrates this into the App Router so streaming works without additional configuration.

node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:36:When a browser requests a page, two streams work together during the initial page load:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:37:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:38:### The HTML stream
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:39:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:40:React's server renderer produces progressive HTML chunks. The static parts of your page (layouts, navigation, Suspense fallbacks) render first and are sent immediately. When an async [Server Component](/docs/app/glossary#server-component) resolves, React streams its completed HTML along with inline `<script>` tags: one that swaps the fallback DOM node with the new content, and another carrying the [component payload](#the-component-payload) so React can later hydrate it. The browser executes the swap instantly, without waiting for the page's JavaScript bundle to load or hydration to complete. This is what the user _sees_: the page painting progressively, section by section.
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:41:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:42:### The component payload
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:43:
node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:44:The component payload is a serialized representation of the component tree that React uses to [hydrate](/docs/app/glossary#hydration) the page and handle client-side updates. On initial load, it arrives embedded in the HTML stream (as described above). On **client-side navigation**, only the component payload is fetched (with an `rsc: 1` request header) and no HTML is transferred at all. React uses it to update the component tree in place.

node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:46:### The static shell

node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:48:Everything that renders before any async work resolves is called the **static shell**: your layouts, navigation, and the fallback UI defined by your `<Suspense>` boundaries. It is sent immediately, giving the user something to see and interact with while dynamic content streams in. With [Cache Components](/docs/app/getting-started/caching), the static shell is prerendered at build time and served instantly from the edge.

node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:374:|                | `loading.js`                             | `<Suspense>`                     |

node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/streaming.md:381:Prefer explicit `<Suspense>` boundaries close to the dynamic access. When the prerenderer encounters dynamic work, it walks up the tree looking for the nearest Suspense boundary. If none is found, the build fails with a [blocking route error](/docs/messages/blocking-route). A `loading.js` high in the tree is a valid boundary, so the framework finds it and stops, but now the entire page falls back to a full-page skeleton instead of streaming granularly.
